abstract: The μ-opioid receptor (MOR), encoded by Oprm1, mediates both the pain-relieving and addictive effects of opioids. Despite the key role of cerebral cortex in pain perception and motivated behaviors, the identity of MOR-expressing cortical neurons remains unclear. To address this, we used intersectional genetic tools, single-cell RNA sequencing, viral tracing, and electrophysiology to characterize Oprm1-expressing neurons in the mouse cortex. We find Oprm1 expression in an assembly of inhibitory and pyramidal neuron subtypes preferentially located in deep layers, projecting to distinct thalamic nuclei and intracortically to layer 1. Furthermore, Oprm1+ neurons are concentrated in lateral areas, including the somatosensory cortex, rather than in medial prefrontal areas. This challenges prior assumptions, suggesting that MOR abundance in the medial prefrontal cortex may originate from thalamic inputs rather than local neurons. These findings define opioid-sensitive cortical circuits to study their contributions to opioid analgesia and addiction.
